RANDOM STRATA · BETA

Random, with a structure.

These four palettes were supplied by Coonie after a Gemini-assisted experiment. Their intended 32×32 layout has sixteen 8×8 sections: one random grayscale section and fifteen 24° HSV hue sectors. Each colored section calls for eight fully saturated, full-value colors, then fourteen samples from each of four saturation/value quadrants.

The supplied RGB values are preserved exactly. “Beta” distinguishes their actual colors from the stricter distance rule in the original prompt. The generator implementation was not supplied, so the audits describe the outputs without assuming why the rule was missed.

Distances use CIEDE2000 in CIELAB D65/2°, with kL = kC = kH = 1, measured on the final 8-bit sRGB values. A palette's minimum is its closest pair, not its typical spacing or its image-mapping error.

Four trials, one 4,096-color palette

The 4,096 source entries contain 3,949 unique colors: 3,777 colored entries and 172 grays. The 147 repeated occurrences divide into 84 grays and 63 colored entries. The combined beta includes every original unique color, all 256 true sRGB grays, and 63 new colored samples.

The new samples are chosen by deterministic farthest-point CIEDE2000 selection from random candidates stratified over the same fifteen hue sectors and four S/V quadrants, plus vivid candidates. Every new colored sample is at least 4.669 ΔE00 from every other final color. Existing close pairs and the deliberately complete grayscale remain intact.

Try 1 occupies the upper left, Try 2 upper right, Try 3 lower left, and Try 4 lower right. Only repeated occurrences are replaced: missing gray levels occupy duplicate gray cells, and new colored samples occupy duplicate colored cells. Those filled cells are chosen for coverage and do not retain the original cell's hue-sector quota.

Generator v2: adaptive vivid rows and near-grays

The updated generator keeps the 32×32 layout and all original section counts. The first block now samples the entire 15,436-color near-gray pool: max(R,G,B) − min(R,G,B) ≤ 4 in integer byte RGB. #000000 and #ffffff are forced; 62 more near-grays fill that block. Every hue-block sample must be outside this region, checked after rounding.

This widened pool can support the global target: the tested seed-42 palette has a gray–gray minimum of 2.5045 ΔE00, including the forced endpoints. If a configured gray distance cannot be reached within the retry budget, the script reports failure rather than silently lowering it.

Each hue sector gets its own vivid-row target. The script enumerates every possible fully saturated, full-value byte RGB in that sector, then uses an exact eight-point compatibility search. If eight colors fit at the global target (2.5 by default), it stops there. Otherwise it finds the maximum feasible separation and subtracts 0.2 ΔE00 by default for variation. When that margin would exceed half the maximum, it is limited to half, keeping the target positive.

Sector order and the chosen eight-point sets are randomized. Each maximum is conditional on previously selected vivid colors, and is exact for those conditions—not a claim of a globally optimal simultaneous allocation across all fifteen sectors. A vivid pair uses the smaller of its two sector targets, including across sector boundaries. Every pair involving a quadrant sample, and gray–vivid pairs, keeps the global target.

Run with just an output filename. No third-party Python packages are needed:

python3 generate-random-strata.py palette.gpl

Each run gets a fresh random seed, recorded in its audit. Use a seed to reproduce a palette:

python3 generate-random-strata.py palette.png --seed 42

For more room to vary the vivid rows in constrained sectors:

python3 generate-random-strata.py palette.gpl --vivid-margin 0.35

The margin only applies when the global cap cannot be met; sectors that reach it keep that target. --min-distance changes the global target. The optional --gray-distance changes gray–gray spacing explicitly; --vivid-distance supplies an optional lower cap for the adaptive vivid rows. Neither flag is needed for the default run.

The complete example contains 1,024 unique colors and zero violations of its configured rules. Its smallest distance is about 0.1937 ΔE00 in the vivid rows; the near-gray minimum is 2.5045, and all other pair classes exceed 2.5.

Output supports .gpl, .txt, .hex, .json and .png. PNG is 32×32 RGB without alpha. Every successful run writes an audit JSON sidecar. --check-only reports independent sector capacities before interactions with other sectors; actual run targets may differ. Generation has bounded restarts and per-slot retry limits. A failed random search is reported as a search failure, not proof of impossibility.

The CIEDE2000 function passes all 34 bundled reference cases. The exact eight-point solver is also checked against exhaustive small-graph solutions, and the output is independently audited using the project's NumPy implementation. The five beta palettes above remain the supplied experiments and their combined union; the generator and example downloads are now v2.
